title: SLA-margin-buffer-staircase-planner-q1-2027
body:
Purpose:
A lightweight financial model for mapping per-region SLA margin cushions to a headcount
staircase (hiring steps) and operational gating triggers. Designed for product and ops to
agree on explicit thresholds (price, latency SLO breaches, token-cost delta) that change hiring
plan cadence and enable short-term burst reserves. This is intentionally pragmatic — a single
page sheet with scenario toggles and a small sensitivity grid.

Executive summary:
- Base case runway: 14.8 months (current burn, committed Dedicated revenue run-rate, and active
  hiring plan).
- Recommended SLA margin buffer: 22% across NA/EU, 18% APAC (buffer = token cost + latency
  insurance + burst reserve).
- Hiring staircase: freeze/slow/normal/accelerate steps tied to price shock and throughput
  thresholds. Each step has defined hiring headcount deltas and time windows.

Assumptions (editable cells):
- Starting monthly burn (opex + committed infra): $3,120,000
- Current committed revenue (monthly): $2,360,000
- Net burn: $760,000
- Average per-token cost (hosted): $0.00028 / token (weighted mix)
- Expected q1 growth in token volume: 12% month-over-month
- Hiring cadence: hires are ramped over 6 weeks to full productivity
- Typical new hire all-in monthly cost (SW Eng / infra): $18,500

Headcount staircase (policy table):
Columns: Step name | Condition | Monthly hire delta | Notes
- Accelerate | ARR growth >= 8% MoM and buffer usage < 8% | +12 hires / month | prioritized infra + SRE
- Normal | baseline (buffer < 18% and price delta < 5%) | +6 hires / month | product + infra mix
- Slow | buffer 18–30% OR price delta 5–12% | +2 hires / month | defer non-critical roles
- Freeze | buffer >= 30% OR price delta > 12% OR 2 consecutive SLA latency P90 breaches | 0 hires; pause contractors | immediate hiring hold + review
- Dehire step | sustained buffer > 45% for 2 months | -6 hires (contractors first) | last-resort wage/role rebalancing

Regional gating policy (per-region buffers and triggers):
- NA: buffer target 22%; trigger freeze if buffer >= 30%; preferred burst: 20% reserved capacity
- EU: buffer target 22%; same freeze trigger but 10% of burst reserved for compliance-heavy customers
- APAC: buffer target 18%; freeze trigger at 28% (due to regional pricing lever flexibility)

Sensitivity grid (price-per-token vs hiring impact):
Columns: price increase | immediate buffer change | runway delta (months) | hiring action
- +0% (base) | 0% | +0 | normal
- +6% | +7% buffer use | -1.2 months | slow
- +11% | +14% buffer use | -2.5 months | slow -> evaluate freeze if coupled with growth slowdown
- +18% | +24% buffer use | -4.9 months | freeze + review dehire options
- +30% | +40% buffer use | -9.8 months | freeze + dehire playbook engaged

Quick scenario examples (auto-calculated rows in sheet):
- Scenario A: high-growth with small price increase
  - Token vol growth: +18% MoM, price +6% -> net revenue delta: +9% -> runway improves by 0.5 months vs base; hire at +8/mo for first 2 months
- Scenario B: price shock with flat demand
  - Token vol growth: 0% MoM, price +18% -> runway shortfall 4.9 months; immediate hiring slow then freeze; place 20% burst capacity on hold

Run-rate math snippet (human-readable):
- Monthly net burn = starting monthly burn - committed revenue +/- one-time adjustments
- Buffer consumption approximated as cumulative incremental infra cost from price delta and added burst ops
- Runway months = cash reserves / monthly net burn (after buffer adjustments and hiring deltas)

Action checklist when trigger fires:
1) Finance: re-run model with latest metered token cost by region (24h).
2) Product/Ops: implement routing policies to favor lower-cost model variants for non-critical routes.
3) Hiring: immediate pause on open requisitions per regional freeze; notify recruiters.
4) Sales: offer temporary usage credits to top 10 customers in affected region to avoid churn.
5) Exec: weekly review cadence until buffer returns under 20% for two consecutive weeks.

Notes / open questions (notes-to-self style):
- Need clearer definition of "buffer usage" calculation; current sheet uses incremental per-token price * expected token consumption; might undercount sustained latency SLO remediation costs (engineering time).
- Consider slotting a small dedicated contingency headcount (2 FTEs) as part of burst reserve rather than pure capex reserve.
- Validate APAC pricing flexibility against cloud vendor committed rates (some committed contracts may not allow quick price pass-through).

Change log:
- 2026-11-02 (Aisha) created base model and assumptions
- 2026-12-15 (Miguel) added regional gating thresholds and sensitivity grid
- 2027-01-12 (Evelyn) refined hiring staircase and added dehire step

Where this lives technically:
- canonical sheet: finance/operational-staircase/SLA-buffer-staircase (linked to Confluence page id CONFL-8942)

Recommended next steps:
- Validate assumptions with SRE (latency remediation cost) and APAC partner ops (contract terms) this week.
- Run three stress test scenarios in the sandbox infra using sampled traffic to estimate actual buffer consumption over a 14-day window.
